Where alert sources are set

Set in /etc/mmhotline/mmhotline_settings.yml, in alert_sources. An administrator edits the settings file with sudoedit, then runs sudo mmhotline settings apply.

Request format and signing

Send signed JSON to the source's Intake URL. The sender uses the signing secret from the team's vault.

{"sender_alert_id":"alert-1","sender_incident_key":"backup","severity":"sos","title":"Backup failed","message":"Disk full"}

Mmhotline-Signature: timestamp_unix_seconds=<unix seconds>,hmac_sha256_hex=<hex HMAC-SHA256>. Decode the 64 hexadecimal characters of the signing secret into 32 bytes, and compute HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a dot, and the exact JSON bytes. The timestamp must be within five minutes. Reuse a sender alert ID when retrying.

An SOS is the urgent alert that wakes the person on call, even at night. A resolved-sos alert with the same sender incident key closes the matching unresolved SOS incident.

A sender that checks in posts a signed message every 30 seconds to the Check-in URL. MMHotline starts watching for missing check-ins after the first check-in arrives.

Times are New York time (America/New_York), the team's time zone.
